title: Comparison of Partial Weight-Bearing vs. Full Weight-Bearing in Postoperative Rehabilitation Following Foot and Ankle Surgery
summary: Following foot or ankle surgery, there are varying recommendations regarding how much weight should be placed on the operated leg during the first few weeks. While some patients are only allowed to bear partial weight on the leg, others can bear full weight on it early on. To date, it remains unclear which of these postoperative management strategies leads to better outcomes. The aim of this study is therefore to investigate how partial or full weight-bearing on the operated leg affects healing, the function of the foot and ankle, pain, quality of life, and the return to work and sports activities. The study is being conducted at a single hospital. Patients are informed about the study during their hospital stay and are given ample opportunity to ask questions. Participation is only permitted with written consent. After the eligibility criteria have been reviewed, participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: a group with partial weight-bearing or a group with full weight-bearing on the operated leg. Immediately after surgery, special sensor insoles are inserted into a medical support boot, which is worn day and night for the first few weeks. During this time, the sensor insoles record the actual load on the operated leg. Follow-up examinations take place six weeks, twelve weeks, and one year after surgery. These examinations assess foot and ankle function, pain, quality of life, potential complications, and bone healing using X-rays. In addition, information is collected regarding the use of pain medication, comorbidities, the duration of work disability, and the return to sports activities. The study aims to help determine the optimal postoperative care following foot and ankle surgery and to improve care for future patients.
conditions: Postoperative care following foot and ankle surgery

interventions.name:
Standard postoperative treatment (Control Group):
- 2 weeks of non-weight-bearing in a walker boot (e.g., Vacoped)
- Followed by 20 kg partial weight-bearing in the walker boot for 4 weeks
- A Loadsole insole is inserted into the walker boot immediately after surgery and records the actual weight

Early functional postoperative treatment (Intervention Group):
- 2 weeks of non-weight-bearing in a walker boot (e.g., Vacoped)
- Followed by full weight-bearing in the walker boot for 4 weeks after confirmed wound healing
- A Loadsole insole is inserted into the walker boot immediately after sur

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients undergoing foot and ankle surgery followed by the above-mentioned postoperative protocol.
Exclusion criteria:
- Polyneuropathy
- Wheelchair dependence
- Dementia
